questions.q: State the integration by parts formula, and explain the LIATE guideline for choosing $u$.
questions.answer: $\int u\,dv = uv-\int v\,du$. LIATE suggests choosing $u$ in the priority order: Logarithmic, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential — the function type listed first should typically be $u$.

questions.q: Derive the integration by parts formula starting from the product rule $\frac{d}{dx}[uv]=u'v+uv'$.
questions.answer: Integrating both sides: $uv=\int u'v\,dx+\int uv'\,dx=\int v\,du+\int u\,dv$. Rearranging: $\int u\,dv=uv-\int v\,du$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int xe^x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=e^x\,dx$: $du=dx$, $v=e^x$. $\int xe^x\,dx = xe^x-\int e^x\,dx = xe^x-e^x+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x\cos x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=\cos x\,dx$: $du=dx$, $v=\sin x$. $\int x\cos x\,dx=x\sin x-\int\sin x\,dx=x\sin x+\cos x+C$.

sections.heading: Integration by parts with logarithms and inverse trig

questions.q: Evaluate $\int \ln x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=dx$: $du=\frac{1}{x}dx$, $v=x$. $\int\ln x\,dx = x\ln x-\int1\,dx = x\ln x-x+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x\ln x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x\,dx$: $du=\frac{1}{x}dx$, $v=\frac{x^2}{2}$. $\int x\ln x\,dx = \frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\int\frac{x}{2}\,dx = \frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^2}{4}+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int \tan^{-1}x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=\tan^{-1}x$, $dv=dx$: $du=\frac{1}{1+x^2}dx$, $v=x$. $\int\tan^{-1}x\,dx = x\tan^{-1}x-\int\frac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx = x\tan^{-1}x-\frac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^2)+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2\ln x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x^2\,dx$: $du=\frac{1}{x}dx$, $v=\frac{x^3}{3}$. $\int x^2\ln x\,dx=\frac{x^3}{3}\ln x-\int\frac{x^2}{3}\,dx=\frac{x^3}{3}\ln x-\frac{x^3}{9}+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int \sin^{-1}x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=\sin^{-1}x$, $dv=dx$: $du=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}dx$, $v=x$. $\int\sin^{-1}x\,dx=x\sin^{-1}x-\int\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx=x\sin^{-1}x+\sqrt{1-x^2}+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2e^x\,dx$, applying integration by parts twice.
questions.answer: First: $u=x^2$, $dv=e^x\,dx$: $\int x^2e^x\,dx = x^2e^x-2\int xe^x\,dx$. Using the earlier result $\int xe^x\,dx=xe^x-e^x$: $=x^2e^x-2(xe^x-e^x)+C = x^2e^x-2xe^x+2e^x+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2\sin x\,dx$, applying integration by parts twice.
questions.answer: First: $u=x^2$, $dv=\sin x\,dx$: $=-x^2\cos x+2\int x\cos x\,dx$. Using the earlier result $\int x\cos x\,dx=x\sin x+\cos x$: $=-x^2\cos x+2x\sin x+2\cos x+C$.

questions.q: Set up (do not evaluate fully) the reduction needed to find $\int x^3e^x\,dx$, identifying how many times integration by parts must be applied.
questions.answer: Each application of IBP with $u=x^n$ reduces the power of $x$ by $1$ while $v$ stays an antiderivative of $e^x$. Since the power starts at $3$, integration by parts must be applied $3$ times to eliminate the polynomial factor entirely.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int e^x\sin x\,dx$ using the cyclic (solve-for-the-integral) technique.
questions.answer: Let $I=\int e^x\sin x\,dx$. First IBP ($u=\sin x$, $dv=e^x dx$): $I=e^x\sin x-\int e^x\cos x\,dx$. Second IBP on the remaining integral ($u=\cos x$, $dv=e^xdx$): $\int e^x\cos x\,dx=e^x\cos x+\int e^x\sin x\,dx=e^x\cos x+I$. So $I=e^x\sin x-(e^x\cos x+I) \Rightarrow 2I=e^x\sin x-e^x\cos x \Rightarrow I=\frac{e^x(\sin x-\cos x)}{2}+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int e^{2x}\cos x\,dx$ using the cyclic technique.
questions.answer: Let $I=\int e^{2x}\cos x\,dx$. IBP ($u=\cos x$, $dv=e^{2x}dx$): $I=\frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos x+\frac{1}{2}\int e^{2x}\sin x\,dx$. IBP again on that integral ($u=\sin x$, $dv=e^{2x}dx$): $\int e^{2x}\sin x\,dx=\frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\sin x-\frac{1}{2}I$. Substituting: $I=\frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos x+\frac{1}{4}e^{2x}\sin x-\frac{1}{4}I \Rightarrow \frac{5}{4}I=\frac{1}{2}e^{2x}\cos x+\frac{1}{4}e^{2x}\sin x \Rightarrow I=\frac{e^{2x}(2\cos x+\sin x)}{5}+C$.

sections.heading: Definite integrals using integration by parts

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_0^1 xe^x\,dx$ using the antiderivative found earlier.
Evaluate $\int_1^e \ln x\,dx$ using the antiderivative found earlier.
Evaluate $\int_0^{\pi} x\sin x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=\sin x\,dx$: $\int x\sin x\,dx=-x\cos x+\int\cos x\,dx=-x\cos x+\sin x+C$. $\left[-x\cos x+\sin x\right]_0^{\pi}=(-\pi(-1)+0)-(0+0)=\pi$.

sections.heading: Integration by parts to derive a reduction formula

questions.q: Use integration by parts to show $\int x^ne^x\,dx=x^ne^x-n\int x^{n-1}e^x\,dx$ (the reduction formula), and use it once to reconfirm $\int x^2e^x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=x^n$, $dv=e^x\,dx$: $du=nx^{n-1}dx$, $v=e^x$. $\int x^ne^x\,dx=x^ne^x-n\int x^{n-1}e^x\,dx$, confirming the reduction formula. With $n=2$: $\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-2\int xe^x\,dx=x^2e^x-2xe^x+2e^x+C$, matching the earlier result.

questions.q: For each integral, state the best choice of $u$ (using LIATE) without evaluating:
Explain what goes wrong if you attempt $\int xe^x\,dx$ with the reversed choice $u=e^x$, $dv=x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Then $du=e^x\,dx$, $v=\frac{x^2}{2}$, giving $\int xe^x\,dx=\frac{x^2}{2}e^x-\int\frac{x^2}{2}e^x\,dx$. The remaining integral is MORE complicated than the original (higher power of $x$ under the same exponential), so this choice makes the problem worse rather than simpler — LIATE's algebraic-before-exponential guidance avoids this trap.

sections.heading: Integration by parts with algebraic-trigonometric products

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x\sec^2x\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=\sec^2x\,dx$: $du=dx$, $v=\tan x$. $\int x\sec^2x\,dx=x\tan x-\int\tan x\,dx=x\tan x+\ln|\cos x|+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int 2x\sin(3x)\,dx$.
questions.answer: Let $u=2x$, $dv=\sin(3x)\,dx$: $du=2\,dx$, $v=-\frac{1}{3}\cos(3x)$. $\int2x\sin(3x)\,dx=-\frac{2x}{3}\cos(3x)+\frac{2}{3}\int\cos(3x)\,dx=-\frac{2x}{3}\cos(3x)+\frac{2}{9}\sin(3x)+C$.

sections.heading: Definite integrals: area under a transcendental product

questions.q: Find the exact area under $y=xe^{-x}$ on $[0,3]$, using $\int xe^{-x}\,dx=-xe^{-x}-e^{-x}+C$ (verify this antiderivative first by differentiating).
Evaluate $\int_0^{\pi/2} x\cos x\,dx$ using the antiderivative $x\sin x+\cos x$ found earlier.
questions.answer: $\left[x\sin x+\cos x\right]_0^{\pi/2}=\left(\frac{\pi}{2}(1)+0\right)-(0+1)=\frac{\pi}{2}-1\approx0.571$.

sections.heading: Mixed review: choosing the right technique

questions.q: For each integral, state whether it should be solved by $u$-substitution or integration by parts, and identify the key choice (substitution variable or $u$) without fully evaluating:
answers: Substitution ($w=x^2$) — the derivative of the exponent is present as a factor
Integration by parts ($u=x^2$, twice) — no matching derivative factor for substitution
Integration by parts ($u=\ln x$) — no simplifying substitution exists here
